page: Amazon Web Services c8i.32xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it features 128 dedicated vCPUs across 64 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, running at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz. The processor is equipped with a 480 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for accelerated matrix and integer operations.

The instance is configured with 256.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory operating at 7 GHz, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local NVMe storage, meaning all storage requirements must be handled via network-attached volumes. Networking capabilities are supported by a baseline bandwidth of 50 Gbps, facilitating high-throughput data transfers.

In benchmark testing, the c8i.32xlarge demonstrates top-tier multi-core performance, ranking in the top 10% for multi-core CPU stress tests, Passmark CPU scores, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. It also excels in memory bandwidth, achieving top-tier results for read-only operations. However, single-core performance is more moderate, placing in the middle 50% for single-core CPU stress tests. The hardware profile is highly cost-efficient for parallelized compute workloads that leverage its dense core count and advanced vector instructions, though workloads requiring massive per-core memory allocations may find the 2.0 GB per core ratio restrictive.

This instance is highly suited for compute-intensive workloads such as software compilation, ray tracing, database operations, and medium-sized LLM inference prompt processing. It is also well-suited for high-throughput static web serving and multi-threaded data compression tasks.
